## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle AoS components with a list-based respawn intermediate can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The AoS Particle struct (68 B/p) plus 4 B/p list intermediate totals 72 B/p. Loop 1 (integrate+decide) touches 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot: age+pos+vel); loop 2 (respawn) touches only 4 of 68 B/p (5% hot: seed); loop 3 (render) touches 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot: color+pos). The 59–95% dead bytes per line are dragged through every fetch. The list intermediate stores death indices for irregular append-based respawn, trading a second full scan for branchy scatter. Working set spills L1d at N≈455 and L2 at N≈7281, so most measured points are L2/L3/DRAM-resident where the low hot fraction wastes cache-line bandwidth.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is nearly flat: 20.9 (L1d, N=320) to 23.3 (L3, N=160K), rising only ~12% across three regimes. No visible knee at the L2 spill (N≈7281) or L3 spill (N≈233K) — cost is frontend-dominated, not capacity-driven. At higher death rates the DRAM transition sharpens: q=0.1 rises from 25.5 (L3) to 30.5 ns/p (DRAM), q=0.25 from 28.2 to 33.8, as respawn scatter amplifies traffic. The dense grid resolves no sharp L2/L3 knee because the algo is never memory-bound.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved BW is 3.44 GB/s (N=320, q=0.01) — 27% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — falling to 2.05 GB/s at q=0.5. The memory floor (5.674 ns/p) frames the gap: at 20.9 ns/p the algo is 3.7x above irreducible memory time, confirming frontend/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Profile: frontend_stall 64–74%, compute 25–35%, branch_flush 0%. Vs baseline: 0.92–1.03x at q=0.01 (tied with naive scalar), deteriorating to 1.05–1.17x worse than naive at q≥0.1 in DRAM. Vs winner: 2.4–3.4x slower at q=0.01, narrowing to 1.86–1.98x at q=0.5.

## Assembly
Loop 1 shows partial 4-wide vectorization: `vmovups` for 16B AoS loads, `vmulps`/`vaddps` for FP, but `vinsertps`/`vshufps` repack components from stride-68B — shuffle overhead negates vector gains. Only 28/426 insns are vector. Loop 2 is 103 insns/iter, 10 cond branches, byte-granular scatter (×10). Loop 4 (render) is 202 insns/iter, 21 cond branches, 12 `cmovae` selects, 16 byte stores via `movzx`+`cmp`+`cmovae`+`mov BYTE PTR` — this scalar byte scatter cannot stream and drives the 64–74% frontend stall. The `vucomiss`+`jb` death check is branchy but well-predicted (branch_flush=0%).

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.92–1.03x of naive at q=0.01 across all N (tied with scalar), and 1.05–1.17x worse than naive at q≥0.1 in DRAM. The partial 4-wide vectorization with `vinsertps` shuffles cannot overcome 64–74% frontend stall from 103–202 insn/iter loops with byte-granular scatter. At 3.7x above the 5.674 ns/p memory floor, the algo is instruction-bound, not bandwidth-bound. The winner is 2.4–3.4x faster at q=0.01 and 1.86–1.98x at q=0.5: the list intermediate's irregular append and byte scatter are the bottleneck.
